not_a_route: Absolute -o on the save-by-name mapper is harmless: the mapper builds f'{models_dir}/{name}', so '/x' lands at <ws>/catalogs/x (tests use '..' spellings there only).
create/replicate/import already refuse a target that is in no trestle project (CreatePathAction); they write into ANY trestle project, so their tests target a sibling workspace.
A leading '..' name is already refused by the name rule (parts[0] starts with '.'); only absolute and inner-'..' spellings get past it.
verified.project_tests_run: fs_test, author/{catalog,prof,ssp,component,headers,docs,folders}_test, create_test, replicate_test, import__test pass offline in the image at the pinned+injected commit except 7 tests that fetch from the internet (deselected in test.sh). test.sh restores pristine copies of these files and runs them in the functional group.
verified.no_leaked_regression_tests: fix commit 37ed44f5 is the direct child of the pinned commit; its fs_test.py additions are absent at the pinned commit and the image drops .git before the agent sees it
verified.outside_fixtures: The unrelated directory is <tmp>/ws-outside and the second workspace <tmp>/ws-neighbour: both share the workspace <tmp>/ws as a string prefix, so a separator-less prefix check is caught (resolved_prefix.patch).

patch_checks.why: the upstream fix as published: the save-by-name mapper, the force-overwrite clear order, names taken from model content and every extra naming option stay open
oracle without the shared name-check hardening (and without the caller adaptation it needs)
the name is judged, but only after the folder has been emptied
the tempting wrong fix: a workspace check in the markdown generate commands only
unresolved string-prefix comparison and a first-component-only '..' rule; '..' after an ordinary first component slips through
the workspace check reduced to a resolved string-prefix comparison without a separator: <tmp>/ws-outside and <tmp>/ws-neighbour count as inside <tmp>/ws
the check validates the model-type folder, not the named model folder
model names checked on lookup, not on save
hardened shared name check while workspace-wide header validation still passes absolute paths: every folder is skipped and bad headers go unreported
over-hardening: any separator refused, nested task/output names break
the shared name check refuses every name
oracle plus NUL/backslash refused in names and the markdown generate outputs judged as well

different design: one realpath/relative_to helper in the shared utilities, a lexical rule in the name check, the judgement in the public save/lookup APIs rather than the private mapper, and the folder cleared only after the name is accepted

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: CLI commands wrap every exception into a non-zero exit, and the tests accept any non-zero exit as long as nothing outside the workspace changed; a crash after the side effect is caught by the side-effect assertion
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: no external authority is consulted; the decision depends only on the name and the workspace path
